newsitem.title: GERMANY: DAG union calls strike ballot at Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: DAG union calls strike ballot at Lufthansa.

text.p: The DAG white collar workers' union said on Monday it had decided to call a strike ballot at German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG in a dispute over pay at the airline.

The DAG, which shares representation of the airline's some 50,000 staff with the OeTV public sector and transport trade union, has already led two limited walk-outs by ground- and aircrews in a dispute over pay with the airline.

In its statement, the union said it had hoped that this action would be enough to persuade the union to reconsider its pay offer. One two-hour strike in December had forced the cancellation of about 90 flights, the union said.

The ballot was set to take place over the next three or four weeks, balloting ground and air crews as well as pilots. The lengthy preparation period was intended to allow flight crews who travelled abroad to participate in the vote.
If a full strike is to go ahead, the union will need to get the support of 70 percent of its members at the airline.
The DAG said it hoped its action would convince Lufthansa to make a one-year pay agreement offering a pay rise in line with others in the sector.

DAG deputy chairman Hubert Gartz said that his union was not prepared to accept a pay agreement running over 27 months as sought by the airline, adding that this was not in line with the performance of the airline's workers.

"The DAG has already proved in the past that it is responsible in its wage policies at Lufthansa and does not lose sight of the competitiveness of the company," he said, referring in particular to pay sacrifices made in 1992.

Lufthansa has offered a one-off payment of 33 percent of a monthly salary to cover the first 1-1/2 years of the proposed contract followed by a 1.7 percent pay rise. The union is seeking a four percent pay increase.
